threads.preview:
That is what I want to hear. Lock it in.

Quick checklist before you touch a bar

paragraphs: Look, you said you were going to get back on the board with a lift, and you got 23 minutes in yesterday morning. It breaks the dry spell. Let me know what you actually hit in that session, what the RPE was, and if we're still locking in another lift this weekend.

messages.text: That was just morning foundation coach

paragraphs: Got it. So that was foundation, not the lift. Which means the dry spell is still live, Sky. You committed to getting one real lift in this weekend before the travel window hits next week. Are we locking in Workout A today or tomorrow?

messages.text: I will do it today coach!

paragraphs:
That is what I want to hear. Lock it in.

Quick checklist before you touch a bar:
1. Single-leg glute bridge on the right in the warm-up. Squeeze before extending.
2. Front lever protocol: SL FL benchmark tested LEFT first, then straddle negatives (25kg band, 5x3 controlled), then SL holds (15kg band, 3x10s).
3. Dips stay at bodyweight with that 3-second eccentric.

Keep it clean, get your numbers down, and tell me how it felt when you're done.

input.message: I don't have a plan for this week yet - go ahead and lay out the full week for me now, nothing unusual going on, just build it around my normal training.

output.reply:
Look, with your trip running Thursday through Sunday, we build around getting your core work done before you leave, then maintaining on the road.

Monday is already logged and won. Today is light recovery. Wednesday is the big home anchor: Workout A. Don't rush it, hit the single-leg glute bridge warm-up for that right hip first. Once you head out Thursday, we shift to travel mobility on flight day, your travel calisthenics routine on Friday, a modified Workout B session Saturday, and a clean reset Sunday when you land.

The entire week is committed to your plan now. Let's make Wednesday count.
